title: Google Maps
summary: Serve map tiles, compute routes and ETAs: pre-rendered vector tiles on a CDN, a road graph partitioned for fast shortest paths, live traffic from location pings, and geocoding.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Render the map at any zoom; search places / addresses (geocoding)
Route from A to B by car/walk/transit with ETA; reroute on traffic
Tile load < 100 ms; route p99 < 1 s

blocks.text: Tiles are static and cacheable; routing is CPU-heavy; traffic ingest is a streaming problem.

items: The world is projected (Web Mercator) and cut into a quadtree of 256×256 tiles: zoom z has 4^z tiles addressed by (z, x, y).
Modern clients fetch **vector tiles** (geometry + labels) and render on device — smaller than raster, restylable, rotatable.
Pre-generate popular zooms; generate deep zooms on demand and cache. Everything is behind a CDN with long TTLs and versioned URLs.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Tiles are a static, content-addressed pyramid — it's a CDN problem, not a database problem.

cols.title: Dijkstra / A*
pros: A* with a distance heuristic cuts work
cons: Too slow on a continental graph for interactive latency

cols.title: Contraction hierarchies / partitioned graphs
pros: Preprocess shortcut edges once; queries touch thousands of nodes instead of millions
Partition into regions with boundary nodes for distributed queries
cons: Preprocessing cost; live traffic weights need customisable variants (e.g. CRP)

items: Edge weights = travel time, from historical speed profiles per time of day blended with live traffic.
ETA = sum of predicted segment times along the route (ML models refine with turn costs, signals, etc.).

items.title: Ingest
items.text: Navigating devices send (lat, lng, speed, ts) every few seconds into a stream (Kafka).

items.title: Map-match
items.text: Snap noisy GPS points to road segments (HMM map matching).

items.title: Aggregate
items.text: Stream processing computes speed per segment over sliding windows.

items.title: Publish
items.text: Update edge weights in routing servers and the traffic overlay tiles every ~minute.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Anonymise and aggregate pings — individual location traces are sensitive.

items: Routing servers hold a regional graph in memory; replicate per region; long routes stitch regions via boundary nodes.
Reroute: client checks deviation; server re-plans from current position.
Offline maps: download a region's tiles + routing graph to the device.

cols.title: Raster tiles
cons: Large; can't restyle or rotate labels

items.title: Scope
items.text: Tiles, search, routing, traffic — pick 2 to go deep.

items.title: Estimate
items.text: Tiles are cacheable; routing is CPU; pings are a stream.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Tile pyramid; CH routing; traffic pipeline.

items.a: 4^18 ≈ 69 billion — which is why deep zooms are generated on demand and mostly empty ocean is skipped.
Parse the address, look it up in an inverted index of address components, rank candidates by match quality and proximity.
A* still explores too many nodes for cross-country routes at interactive latency; preprocessing-based methods answer in milliseconds.

items: Tiles: (z, x, y) quadtree, vector, CDN.
Routing: preprocessed hierarchy in memory, regional.
Traffic: pings → map matching → windowed segment speeds.
ETA = sum of predicted segment times.
